evals.name: outbound-tls-decides-the-image
evals.prompt: In the Kotlin/Native service at {fixture}, add a component that forwards a stored payload to a URL the caller supplies — targets are ordinary https webhook endpoints. Write the code and the build changes. Say anything about this choice a person deploying it should know.
evals.expected_output: ktor-client-cio is identified as having no TLS on Kotlin/Native before it is depended on, not after a failure. Either ktor-client-curl is chosen and its cost to the runtime image is stated, or cio is chosen and the https limitation is stated as a limitation.
expectations: The answer states that ktor-client-cio has no TLS on Kotlin/Native
That statement appears as a reason for the dependency choice, not as a caveat added after proposing cio for https traffic
If ktor-client-curl is chosen, the answer says it links libcurl and therefore changes what the runtime image must carry
The answer does not claim ktor-client-cio will work against an https target
The decision is framed as one to take when the service is created rather than when the first call fails

evals.name: cancellation-is-not-swallowed
evals.prompt: In {fixture}, write a background worker that sweeps the Outbox every second: take what is pending, settle each entry, and keep going. It runs for the life of the process and must stop when its scope is cancelled. A sweep that throws must not kill the worker.
evals.expected_output: The loop catches failures without swallowing CancellationException: either it rethrows CancellationException before catching Throwable, or it uses a form that does not catch cancellation at all. The caught failure is reported rather than discarded.
expectations: CancellationException is not caught and discarded by the loop's error handling
The code either rethrows CancellationException explicitly or uses a construct that never catches it
The failure that is caught is logged, printed or otherwise surfaced, not silently dropped
The answer explains that a bare runCatching or catch (Throwable) around a suspend call would catch cancellation and leave the loop running
The worker's loop condition or structure lets a cancelled scope actually end it

evals.name: native-service-block-before-the-targets
evals.prompt: Convert the build of the service at {fixture} to use the portfolio's sborka conventions, so the binary gets a stable name and a staged path. Do not configure binaries.executable by hand.
evals.expected_output: io.github.youndie.sborka.native-service is applied and the nativeService { entryPoint; baseName } block appears above the kotlin { } block, because the convention reads entryPoint when the target declares its binary.
expectations: The build file applies io.github.youndie.sborka.native-service
The nativeService { } block appears before the kotlin { } block in the file
entryPoint and baseName are set inside nativeService { }
No binaries.executable block is written by hand in the service's own build file
The answer explains that a nativeService block placed after the targets fails with a message naming neither the ordering nor the block

evals.name: health-is-not-readiness
evals.prompt: The service at {fixture} is going into Kubernetes. Wire its health endpoints using the portfolio's kore library and write the probe configuration a chart would use. Explain which probe points where.
evals.expected_output: installKoreProbes is used, and the readiness probe points at /health/ready rather than /health, because /health is an alias for liveness and a readiness probe there cannot fail while the process is alive.
expectations: installKoreProbes is used rather than a hand-written health route
The readiness probe in the chart configuration points at /health/ready
The readiness probe does not point at /health
The answer states that /health is an alias for liveness
The answer explains the consequence: a readiness probe on /health cannot fail while the process is alive

evals.name: nothing-closes-in-applicationstopping
evals.prompt: The service at {fixture} opens a database connection pool at startup. Make sure it is closed cleanly when the process is asked to stop, so no in-flight request loses its connection. Show the wiring.
evals.expected_output: The pool is closed as a kore release-stage participant after the drain, not in an ApplicationStopping handler, because that handler runs before the drain on Kotlin/Native and after it on the JVM from identical source.
expectations: The pool is not closed in an ApplicationStopping or ApplicationStopPreparing handler
The close is registered with kore's shutdown sequence so that it runs after the drain
The answer states that ApplicationStopping runs on opposite sides of the drain on JVM and Kotlin/Native
The answer does not suggest addShutdownHook
runUntilSignal or the shutdown sequence is placed after the server has started serving
